sections.title: The Hook: Dynamics in Motion
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'Rate of Change' vs. 'State'. Use a visual of a rabbit population growing; we don't just see the number of rabbits, but the speed at which the population increases relative to its current size.
sections.example: A rabbit population: The growth rate (dN/dt) is proportional to the current population (N).

sections.title: What is an ODE?
sections.content: Define an ODE as an equation linking a function to its derivatives. Use a graphical split-screen: Left side shows a simple function y=x^2 (static), right side shows dy/dx = 2x (the rule of change). Emphasize that we are solving for a function, not a scalar value.
sections.example: dy/dx = k * y (The classic exponential growth model).

sections.title: Visualizing the Solution: Direction Fields
sections.content: Introduce 'Slope Fields' as the visual landscape of an ODE. Explain that at any point (x, y), the ODE gives us a tiny tangent vector. The solution is the 'path' that follows these vectors, like a stream flowing through a field.
sections.example: Visual animation: A screen filled with small arrows that align to form a curve when a tracer follows them.

sections.title: The Role of Initial Conditions
sections.content: Explain that an ODE defines a family of curves (the 'General Solution'). To find one specific behavior, we need a 'starting point'. Use the analogy of an archer choosing where to stand to dictate the trajectory of an arrow.
sections.example: A falling cat: Starting at height h=10m, with initial velocity v=0.

sections.title: Summary & Real-World Application
sections.content: Recap: ODEs are the language of change. Show a quick montage: a pendulum swinging, a circuit charging, and a planet orbiting. Conclude that mastering ODEs allows us to predict the future state of dynamic systems.
sections.example: The design of a self-driving car's cruise control system using a first-order ODE to maintain constant velocity.

storyboard.title: The Hook: Dynamics in Motion
lecture_lines: Change defines our world, not just static values.
Observe the rabbit population growth over time.
Population speed relates to its current size.
animations: Fade in a title '#FFFFFF' "Rabbit Population Dynamics" at top.
Animate a small rabbit icon spawning into a box.
Show a counter for population size 'N' (color: '#00FF00').
Show a speedometer graphic next to 'N' representing 'dN/dt' (color: '#FF0000').
Flash both icons simultaneously as population size and growth rate change.

storyboard.title: What is an ODE?
lecture_lines: An ODE links a function to its derivative.
We solve for functions, not just numbers.
Take this exponential growth model, for example.
animations: Split screen: Left side label 'Function: y = x^2' (color: '#FFFF00').
Right side label 'ODE: dy/dx = 2x' (color: '#00FFFF').
Draw a static parabola on the left.
Animate a set of tangent arrows along the curve on the right.
Highlight the relationship between the slope of the parabola and the ODE vector field using a connecting line.

storyboard.title: Visualizing the Solution: Direction Fields
lecture_lines: Slope fields show the landscape of change.
Every point dictates a tangent vector's direction.
Follow the stream to visualize the solution.
animations: Populate the screen with a grid of light gray vectors '#808080'.
Color vectors based on angle, creating a gradient field.
Overlay a tracer point at (0,1).
Animate the tracer moving, tracing a curve that stays tangent to the vectors.
Pulse the tracer color '#FFFFFF' as it follows the path.

storyboard.title: The Role of Initial Conditions
lecture_lines: General solutions describe a family of curves.
Initial conditions anchor us to one path.
Like an archer, we pick our starting state.
animations: Display a family of curves in muted color '#555555'.
Place a glowing starting point (initial condition) at (0, 2) in color '#FFD700'.
Draw one specific solution curve passing through that point in color '#00FF00'.
Move the starting point to (0, 5) and watch the curve jump.
Highlight the starting point again to emphasize it dictates the specific path.

storyboard.title: Summary & Real-World Application
lecture_lines: ODEs are the language of dynamic systems.
From pendulums to orbits, we predict change.
Mastering them unlocks the future state.
animations: Montage: Display icons for a pendulum, circuit, and planet.
Animate each icon briefly (swinging, glowing, rotating).
Overlay text: 'Predicting the future state of dynamic systems'.
Flash all icons in sync with the final text pulse.
Fade out all elements to black background '#000000'.
